items.title: Alicia Olatuja interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, February 9, 2018
items.q: I’m influenced by a lot of different musicians and artists... from Joni Mitchell to Imogen Heap... I actually do an encore... in another configuration program called Songs of Freedom, which celebrates songs of Nina Simone, Abbey Lincoln and Joni Mitchell.

ctx.x: Yes, I’m just curious, do you ever take, do you ever look at like contemporary artists and like incorporate bits into your own style from even household names like Beyoncé like you mentioned?

Well I mean it’s great that you mention that because the next album that I just recorded is actually called “Intuition, Songs from the Minds of Women” and it’s celebrating and championing women composers. And I use, I collected a bunch of different songs from women composers of all the genres and backgrounds, from Joni Mitchell to Imogen Heap to Sade, to my student. Like, as well as my own songs as well. But I think hearing the through line of the experience, the human experience is what I’m really going after.…
Yeah I was just listening to your version of “Somewhere Over the Rainbow.” Where do you come up with that?
